rfm_tuples.R: Capital-allocation claim contradiction (HONESTY-ALPHA CATCH). On March 2, 2026, the Board authorized a new $50M share repurchase program through Dec 28, 2030. The 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q BOTH disclose this authorization as a positive shareholder-return signal. HOWEVER: (i) the prior $50M authorization (effective Feb 23, 2024) EXPIRED on Jan 3, 2026 with $50M of UNUSED capacity — i.e., zero shares were repurchased in FY24 or FY25 under the prior authorization, (ii) the new authorization is roll-over of the same $50M amount (not an increase), (iii) at $24/share implied price the new $50M would only retire ~2.6% of the 79.4M shares outstanding, and (iv) capex was simultaneously CUT from $114.8M (FY23) → $95.5M (FY24) → $72.8M (FY25), a 37% reduction over two years, suggesting cash is being conserved rather than deployed.
rfm_tuples.f: If management is genuinely confident in the stock's value at the trough, they should EITHER (a) actually repurchase shares (post-cutoff Q1 2026 10-Q should show repurchases) OR (b) honestly characterize the authorization as a flexible option rather than a return-of-capital commitment. claim_evolution / direct 10-Q read should show whether repurchases actually occurred Q1 2026.

As of April 4, 2026, the authorization has remaining capacity of $50 million.' = ZERO shares repurchased in Q1 2026, despite the stock being within 2% of its 52-week low. FY24 + FY25 + Q1 2026 cumulative repurchase activity under the SUBSEQUENT $50M auths = $0. The only repurchases during the entire 3-year period were the $25M done in FY23 (1.1M shares) under the ORIGINAL February 2022 authorization.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is a classic 'authorization theater' pattern — three consecutive years (FY24, FY25, Q1 FY26) of zero buyback execution despite (a) two consecutive $50M authorizations, (b) the stock trading at the lowest level since the 2017 IPO, and (c) operating cash flow growing to $146M. The 10-K and Q1 10-Q both treat the new $50M authorization as a meaningful capital-return event, but the historical execution rate is 0%. Combined with the simultaneous 37% capex cut (from $114.8M → $72.8M FY23-FY25), the implied capital-allocation framework is: 'We are conserving cash to delever Term Loan A ($237.6M due June 2028, variable SOFR+~2%) and to refinance, NOT to return to shareholders.' The under-delivery is the rhetorical-vs-actual mismatch: the buyback authorization is presented as shareholder-friendly, but the company's revealed preference is balance-sheet defense ahead of the 2028 maturity. MODERATE because the facts are disclosed (zero shares bought is in the table) but the strategic framing in management commentary obscures the gap between authorization and execution.

summary: EYE is a 1,250-store, $1.99B-revenue value-segment optical retailer (America's Best 1,057, Eyeglass World 122, Vista Optical/Military 53, Vista Optical/Fred Meyer 18) with: (i) NO going-concern language and a 24-year Deloitte auditor tenure (CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE / NO_GOING_CONCERN), (ii) a fully resolved litigation overhang — Securities Class Action dismissed March 2024 / reconsideration denied March 2025 / no appeal; Derivative Action dismissed Feb 2026 / not appealed by March 13 2026 deadline / Q1 10-Q confirms 'matter is now closed'; California PAGA $4.6M settled Oct 2025, (iii) the Walmart partnership cleanly wound down as discontinued operations in FY24 with no obscuring (38 EDGAR hits all consistent with wind-down narrative; megacap_namecheck confirms Walmart no longer references NVI), (iv) routine 10b5-1 insider activity (ROUTINE_10B5_1; $11.4M aggregate over 365 days, n_discretionary_proximate=0), (v) FY25 net income recovery to $29.6M (vs $(28.5)M FY24 / $(65.9)M FY23) with comparable store sales accelerating (America's Best +6.3%, Eyeglass World +4.2%), and (vi) manageable secured debt ($237.6M Term Loan A due June 2028, 42% hedged, $293.3M undrawn revolver). The -41.9% drawdown to 2% above 52-week low is NOT a fraud, solvency, or auditor-distress story. The three HONESTY-ALPHA catches are: (C3) Eyeglass World 'brand positioning review' announced in 10-K but ZERO progress disclosure in the very next Q1 2026 10-Q — a still-live serial-impairment-risk brand without a tracking mechanism, (C5) 86% lens-supplier concentration disclosed numerically but without naming the vendor, contract term, or mitigation strategy, and (C7) 'authorization theater' — three consecutive years of zero buyback execution despite two consecutive $50M authorizations and stock at trough, masking a capital-allocation reality of cash-conservation ahead of June 2028 Term Loan A maturity rather than shareholder return. Composite 0.375 across 8 verifiable claims (5 PASS / 3 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 0 RED FLAG / 0 UNVERIFIABLE).
